correctness.rationale: On the event a vertex is isolated, all remaining iid uniform positions lie in a single complementary arc of length L=1-2r; the circular wrap-around distance is at least 2r>r, so an edge among the other vertices occurs with probability q=1-((L-r)_+/L)^2. The conditional edge expectation and exchangeability prove (1); exact polynomial factorization proves (2). Discriminants and the monotone high-radius branch exhaust the n and r ranges, including n=6 and r=1/3 boundaries. The n*r=c asymptotic uses L^n->e^-2c and the polynomial limit. A script verified 15,252 exact rational identities plus five direct graph simulations; these are checks, not substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The statistic pair is canonical for spatial network formation: edge count measures aggregate contact, isolates determine a connectivity obstruction. Despite the same edge marginal as an Erdos-Renyi graph (where covariance is always negative), geometric clustering produces a positive interval only from n=6 onward. Two exact sign transitions, including threshold c=4/3 in the natural sparse regime, characterize when local vacancy and global edge density compete. This is more than a rescaling or a single computational sample.
